mainTopic: Donated oil and donated wine: how much of each is burned on the מזבח, and whether sprinkling wine on the fire counts as putting it out.
overview: שמואל rules that according to רבי טרפון, donated oil is treated like a מנחה: a קומץ is burned and the rest is eaten. He learns this from the words "קרבן מנחה". רבי זירא and אביי read two clauses of a teaching of רבי שמעון in opposite ways. The גמרא shows how each of them can explain the clause that seems to go against him. רב פפא then links שמואל to a dispute between תנאים over whether donated oil is one לוג or three. The רבנן compare oil to a מנחה in every way. רבי learns from מנחה only that oil can be donated, and treats it like נסכים in every other way, so all of it is burned. Next, שמואל rules that donated wine is sprinkled on the altar fires, and the גמרא defends this against the ban on putting out the altar fire. In the end it says שמואל follows רבי שמעון, who allows an action when the forbidden result is not intended. The amud closes by asking whether שמואל really holds like רבי שמעון, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל: Donated oil is handled like a meal offering
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that according to רבי טרפון, donated oil has a קומץ taken from it, and its שיריים are eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: According to רבי טרפון, if a person donates oil, a handful is taken from it, and the rest is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ruling of שמואל about what happens to oil that a person donates by itself, following רבי טרפון's view in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון holds that a person may donate plain oil as its own offering. שמואל adds how it is offered: it is treated like a מנחה. A handful goes on the מזבח, and the כהנים eat the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows the משנה
One who donates a voluntary offering
The handful the כהן removes and burns on the מזבח
The remainder after the קומץ is taken, eaten by כהנים

phrases.english: GEMARA: Shmuel said:
According to the words of Rabbi Tarfon,
one who donates oil –
a handful is taken from it, and its remainder is eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי טרפון, donated oil has a קומץ burned and its שיריים eaten.

steps.title: What is the source for שמואל's ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind שמואל's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where שמואל gets his rule. This sets up the next step, where a פסוק is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not an attack. It is a request for the source that shows donated oil is treated like a מנחה.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of step 1
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for treating donated oil like a מנחה

steps.title: The פסוק "קרבן מנחה" compares oil to a מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The words "קרבן מנחה" teach two things: oil may be donated, and it follows the rules of a מנחה, so a קומץ is burned and the rest is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says "קרבן מנחה". This teaches that one may donate oil, and that it is like a מנחה. Just as a מנחה has a handful taken and the rest eaten, so too oil has a handful taken and the rest eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. The word "קרבן" next to "מנחה" shows that oil can be donated, and it puts that oil in the same group as a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word "קרבן" is read as including donated oil. Because the פסוק links it to "מנחה", the oil copies how a מנחה is offered: a קומץ goes on the fire and the שיריים are eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering of a meal offering (ויקרא 2:1)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: according to רבי טרפון, donated oil is like a מנחה. A קומץ is burned and the שיריים are eaten.

phrases.english: The verse said: "an offering of a meal offering" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:1. The word קרבן seems extra, so it is read as adding oil.

phrases.english: it teaches that one may donate oil;
and it is like a meal offering:
just as a meal offering has a handful taken and its remainder eaten,
so too oil has a handful taken and its remainder eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words "קרבן מנחה" include donated oil and compare it to a מנחה.

steps.title: רבי זירא finds support in רבי שמעון's first clause
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא brings רבי שמעון's teaching. Oil shared out in the עזרה can only be leftover oil, because oil cannot be donated. So the one who says oil can be donated holds that it is shared out, as שמואל said.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: We also learned this. רבי שמעון said: If you see oil being shared out in the courtyard, you do not need to ask what it is. It is leftover oil from the wafers of Israelites' meal offerings, or the log of oil of a מצורע, because one cannot donate oil. This implies that according to the one who says one can donate oil, that oil is also shared out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא tries to prove שמואל right from a teaching of רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that oil cannot be donated, so any oil being eaten must come from somewhere else. He explains it this way because he rejects donation. That suggests that according to רבי טרפון, who allows donation, donated oil would also be eaten. This fits שמואל's rule that the שיריים are eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: Shared out among כהנים to eat
The measure of oil brought by a healed מצורע

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
We too have also learned this:
Rabbi Shimon said:
If you saw oil
that is being shared out in the courtyard –
you do not need to ask what it is;
rather, it is leftover oil from the wafers of Israelites' meal offerings
or the log of oil of a leper,
because one does not donate oil.
This implies that according to the one who says one may donate –
it is shared out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for שמואל's ruling
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that donated oil is eaten by כהנים (its שיריים)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first clause of רבי שמעון's teaching about oil being shared out in the עזרה

steps.title: אביי: The last clause implies donated oil is all burned
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes the last clause. Oil placed on the fires is leftover oil from כהנים' offerings, because oil cannot be donated. This implies that according to the one who allows donation, all of it goes on the fires.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Say the last clause. If you see oil being put on the fires, you do not need to ask what it is. It is leftover oil from the wafers of כהנים' meal offerings, or from the meal offering of the כהן משיח, because one cannot donate oil. This implies that according to the one who says one can donate oil, all of it goes on the fires.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבי זירא by reading the last clause of the same teaching, which seems to point the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי שמעון says burned oil must come from כהנים' offerings only because donation is impossible, then according to רבי טרפון, donated oil would be burned. אביי reads this as all of it being burned, which goes against שמואל's rule that the rest is eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן's meal offering, which is burned completely

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: Say the last clause:
If you saw oil
that is placed on the fires –
you do not need to ask what it is;
rather, it is leftover oil from the wafers of priests' meal offerings
or from the meal offering of the anointed priest,
because one does not donate oil.
This implies that according to the one who says one may donate –
all of it goes to the fires.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's proof using the same teaching
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's proof and שמואל's rule that the שיריים are eaten
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The last clause implies that donated oil is completely burned, not shared out.

steps.title: Each reading has a problem with one clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the first clause is a problem for אביי, and the last clause is a problem for רבי זירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: For אביי, the first clause is difficult. For רבי זירא, the last clause is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the two clauses seem to contradict each other, so each אמורא has one clause that works against him. This sets up the attempts to resolve it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause hints that donated oil is eaten, which goes against אביי. The last clause hints that it is burned, which goes against רבי זירא. Each side now has to explain away one clause.

phrases.english: For Abaye, the first clause is difficult;
for Rabbi Zeira, the last clause is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַבָּיֵי קַשְׁיָא רֵישָׁא, לְרַבִּי זֵירָא קַשְׁיָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the problem created by steps 4 and 5
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two clauses of רבי שמעון's teaching seem to point in opposite directions.

steps.title: רבי זירא can fit both clauses
steps.stepSummary: For רבי זירא there is no real problem. The first clause is about the שיריים, which are eaten, and the last clause is about the קומץ, which is burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רבי זירא: the first clause is about the remainder, and the last clause is about the handful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי זירא's view fits both clauses at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following שמואל, donated oil is split: the קומץ is burned and the שיריים are eaten. So the burned oil of the last clause is the handful, and the eaten oil of the first clause is the remainder. Nothing contradicts.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Zeira –
the first clause is about the remainder, the last clause about the handful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty for רבי זירא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each clause refers to a different part of the oil
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The last clause disproves שמואל, since it implies the oil is burned
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the קומץ is burned, which fits שמואל

steps.title: But אביי still has a problem
steps.stepSummary: For אביי, who holds all the oil is burned, the first clause still seems to contradict him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to אביי, it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses אביי. He cannot use רבי זירא's split, so he needs a different answer for the first clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי says donated oil is burned completely, so no part of it is eaten. That leaves the first clause, which hints that donated oil is shared out, unexplained.

phrases.english: But according to Abaye – it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 7: אביי cannot use the same answer
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading that donated oil is completely burned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first clause implies donated oil is shared out, and אביי has no remainder to apply it to.

steps.title: The first clause was worded to match the last clause
steps.stepSummary: The first clause was only phrased in parallel to the last clause, so nothing should be learned from its wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first clause was taught because of the last clause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for אביי: the first clause's wording is just a style that matches the last clause, so no inference can be drawn from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real point is in the last clause. The first clause was written in the same pattern ("you do not need to ask, because one does not donate") for balance. So the hint that donated oil is shared out is not meant, and אביי's reading stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause was taught because of the last clause

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא: donated oil follows שמואל, with a קומץ burned and the rest eaten, and both clauses fit. אביי: all of it is burned, and the first clause is only worded to match the last.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think אביי denies that רבי שמעון said the first clause. He agrees it is there, but holds that its wording is only for balance and teaches nothing about donated oil.

phrases.english: He taught the first clause because of the last clause.
phrases.notes: He means the first clause copies the pattern of the last one, so don't read anything into its wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty against אביי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Wording is only stylistic: no inference from the first clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first clause implies donated oil is shared out, against אביי
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause's wording only matches the last clause, so אביי's reading holds

steps.title: Would a תנא word the first clause because of the last?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי's answer. It is normal to word a later clause to match an earlier one, but is it normal to word an earlier clause to match a later one?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that a later line is worded to match an earlier line. But would a teacher word the earlier line to match a line that comes after it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer it just gave for אביי, that the first clause was only worded to match the last clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A teacher naturally copies wording he has already used. Copying wording he has not said yet is unusual. So the answer given for אביי looks weak.

phrases.english: It makes sense that the last clause is taught in a certain way because of the first clause;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רֵישָׁא מִשּׁוּם סֵיפָא מִי תָּנֵי?!
phrases.english: but would he teach the first clause in a certain way because of the last clause?!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא סֵיפָא תָּנֵי מִשּׁוּם רֵישָׁא אֶלָּא רֵישָׁא מִשּׁוּם סֵיפָא מִי תָּנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer for אביי that the first clause only copies the wording of the last clause.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wording usually carries forward from earlier clauses to later ones, not backward.

steps.title: Yes, in ארץ ישראל they say a first clause can follow the last
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the scholars in ארץ ישראל do say the first clause is sometimes worded because of the last clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. In the West (ארץ ישראל) they say: the teacher worded the first clause to match the last clause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי's answer. Wording the first clause to match the last clause is an accepted idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer leans on a known approach from ארץ ישראל, so the answer for אביי stands. Nothing can be proven from the wording of the first clause.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: The first clause does not prove anything against אביי. It may simply be worded to match the last clause.

phrases.english: Yes; they say in the West:
He taught the first clause because of the last clause.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings outside support for an unusual way of wording a source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A teacher would never shape an earlier clause to match a later one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The scholars of ארץ ישראל accept that this does happen, so אביי's answer holds.

steps.title: A ברייתא about donated wine and oil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: donated wine goes into the basins and donated oil goes onto the fires. Since all the wine goes into the basins, it seems all the oil is burned too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Wine, following רבי עקיבא, goes into the basins. Oil, following רבי טרפון, goes onto the fires. Doesn't this mean that just as all the wine goes into the basins, all the oil goes onto the fires?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source that seems to show that donated oil is burned completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts wine and oil side by side. All the wine is poured into the basins, so the same should be true of the oil: all of it is burned. That goes against the view that only a handful is burned and the rest is eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: Basins at the corner of the מזבח where wine was poured

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Wine, according to the words of Rabbi Akiva, goes into the basins;
oil, according to the words of Rabbi Tarfon, goes onto the fires.
What, is it not that since the wine all goes into the basins,
the oil also all goes onto the fires?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source into the debate over what happens to donated oil.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that donated oil has a handful burned and the rest eaten.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists wine and oil side by side, so the oil should be used up completely just like the wine.

steps.title: Wine and oil need not follow the same rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: each case follows its own rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they really the same? This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting wine and oil next to each other in one ברייתא does not mean they work the same way. Wine can go entirely into the basins, while oil can still have just a handful burned.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this comparable? (are the cases really alike?)
This is as it is, and that is as it is

phrases.english: Are the cases comparable?
This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge brought in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between wine and oil.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Being listed together does not mean being treated the same.

steps.title: רב פפא: this matches a dispute about the amount of oil
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the question matches a dispute between תנאים. The תנא קמא says donated oil must be at least one לוג, and רבי says three לוגין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: this is like a dispute between תנאים. Oil: one should not bring less than a לוג. רבי says: three לוגין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא ties the question about donated oil to an older dispute between תנאים over the minimum amount one may donate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא was arguing from sources. Now רב פפא shows that תנאים already argued about this, through a disagreement on how much oil must be brought. The reasons behind each side are explained in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: it is like a dispute between תנאים:
Oil: one should not bring less than a לוג.
Rabbi says: three לוגין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from arguing over sources to showing an older dispute between תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The minimum donation of oil is one לוג according to the תנא קמא, and three לוגין according to רבי.

steps.title: What is the root of their dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle the two תנאים are arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question. The גמרא is getting ready to explain the reasoning behind each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants the principle behind the numbers one לוג and three לוגין, not just the numbers themselves.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the dispute quoted in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that splits the תנא קמא and רבי.

steps.title: Learning from one case: in every way, or in one way only
steps.stepSummary: The Sages tell רב פפא that the dispute is about how far a comparison reaches. One view says 'learn from it, and fully from it'. The other says 'learn from it, but keep the rest in its own place'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said before רב פפא: the difference between them is whether we say 'learn from it, and fully from it' or 'learn from it, and set it in its own place'.
steps.whatsHappening: The Sages explain that the two תנאים argue about how fully donated oil is compared to a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Donated oil is learned from מנחה. If we learn 'fully from it', oil copies all the rules of a מנחה. If we 'set it in its own place', we learn only the basic point that oil can be donated, and its other rules come from its own category.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, and fully from it: copy all the rules of the source
Learn from it, but keep the rest in its own place: copy only the main point
That is the difference between them

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that oil is learned from מנחה. They argue only about how much of the מנחה's rules carry over.

phrases.english: The Sages said it before Rav Pappa:
"Learn from it, and fully from it"
versus "learn from it, and set it in its own place"
is the difference between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue whether a comparison carries over every rule or only the main point.

steps.title: The רבנן compare donated oil to a מנחה in every way
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן follow 'learn from it, and fully from it'. Oil can be donated like a מנחה, it takes a לוג like a מנחה, and like a מנחה a handful is burned and the rest is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold: just as a מנחה can be donated, oil can be donated. And from that same source: just as a מנחה uses a לוג of oil, here too a לוג of oil. And just as a מנחה has a handful taken and the rest eaten, oil too has a handful taken and the rest eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the view of the רבנן, the תנא קמא, who compare donated oil to a מנחה in every detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the רבנן learn 'fully from it', every rule of the מנחה carries over to oil. That explains their minimum of one לוג. It also means a handful is burned and the rest is eaten, which matches שמואל's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: One may donate it as a voluntary offering
The handful taken out and burned
The leftover part, eaten by the כהנים

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, donated oil follows the מנחה in every way: one לוג, a handful burned, and the rest eaten.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the view that the oil's leftover is eaten has a source among the תנאים.

phrases.english: For the Rabbis hold:
Just as a מנחה can be donated,
so too oil can be donated;
[and again from it: just as a מנחה has a לוג of oil,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording of the text.

phrases.english: so too here, a לוג of oil.
And just as a מנחה has a handful taken out and its leftover is eaten,
so too oil has a handful taken out and its leftover is eaten.]

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the principle from step 16 to the view of the רבנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן copy all the rules of מנחה to oil: it can be donated, it takes one לוג, and a handful is burned while the rest is eaten.

steps.title: רבי: donate oil like a מנחה, but treat it like נסכים
steps.stepSummary: רבי learns from מנחה only that oil can be donated. Otherwise oil follows the rules of נסכים: three לוגין, and all of it goes to the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי) learns from a מנחה: just as a מנחה can be donated, oil can be donated too. But then he keeps it in its own place, like נסכים: just as נסכים are three לוגין, oil is three לוגין. And just as נסכים go entirely into the basins, oil goes entirely onto the fires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains רבי's side, using the rule 'learn from it, but keep the rest in its own place'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי borrows only one detail from מנחה: oil can be donated. For every other detail, oil is treated like wine נסכים, which are also poured on the altar. That is why רבי says three לוגין and not one, and why none of the oil is eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, but keep the rest in its own place
Wine libations poured on the altar
Basins on the altar that the libations are poured into

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two views. The רבנן copy everything from מנחה, so the oil is one לוג and some is eaten. רבי copies only 'it can be donated', so the oil is three לוגין and all of it is burned.

phrases.english: And the other one learns from a meal offering:
phrases.notes: 'The other one' is רבי, who said three לוגין back in step 14.

phrases.english: just as a meal offering may be donated,
so too oil may be donated;
and keep it in its own place, like libations:
just as libations are three log,
so too oil is three log,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording. Inside them, read שְׁלֹשָׁה and leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: and just as libations go entirely into the basins,
so too oil goes entirely onto the fires.
phrases.notes: Read כּוּלּוֹ, 'all of it', meaning the oil. The round-bracket word is left out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other half of the answer from step 16, after step 17 explained the רבנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי learns only donation from מנחה. Amount and burning follow נסכים: three לוגין, all of it on the fires.

steps.title: רב פפא: everyone accepts 'learn fully from it'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא argues that if רבי learned from מנחה, he too would copy everything from it, since everyone accepts 'learn from it, and fully from it' here.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: If רבי brought it from מנחה, everyone holds 'learn from it, and fully from it'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on the explanation just given for רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא holds that once oil is learned from מנחה, everyone would copy all the details of מנחה. So the reasoning in step 18 cannot be how רבי gets three לוגין.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, and fully from it: copy every detail
He brings it, meaning he learns it from a source

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
If Rebbi derives it from the meal offering,
phrases.notes: The word רבי in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: then everyone holds 'learn from it, and fully from it'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: אִי מִמִּנְחָה מַיְיתֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the way step 18 explained רבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי learns oil from מנחה and uses 'keep it in its own place'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the source is מנחה, all agree to copy every detail. Then רבי would hold one לוג, not three.

steps.title: רב פפא: רבי learns it from 'אזרח'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא suggests that רבי learns donated oil from the word 'אזרח' in the section about נסכים, so it follows the rules of נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי learns it from 'אזרח'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives his own explanation of where רבי gets his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי's source is a פסוק about נסכים and not about מנחה, it makes sense that oil follows נסכים: three לוגין, all burned. This avoids the problem raised in step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Homeborn', a word in the Torah's section on libations

phrases.english: Rather, Rebbi
learns it from 'homeborn'.
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:13, in the section about libations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב פפא answers his own challenge with a different source for רבי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the source of the derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי learns oil from מנחה but limits the comparison.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי learns oil from 'אזרח', a נסכים verse, so it naturally follows נסכים.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי learns it from 'קרבן'
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן brings a ברייתא that learns donated oil from 'קרבן מנחה' and still says three לוגין. Since that is רבי's view, רבי does learn from מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן said to רב פפא: Can you really say that? A ברייתא teaches: 'קרבן מנחה' teaches that one may donate oil. How much? Three לוגין. Who says three לוגין? רבי! And he learns it from 'קרבן'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא challenges רב פפא's explanation with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says three לוגין, which is רבי's number, and gets donated oil from the word 'קרבן' in the מנחה section. That proves רבי does learn from מנחה, not from 'אזרח', and so the explanation in step 18 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Whom have you heard say this?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Natan said to Rav Pappa:
Can you really say that?!
But it is taught: 'a meal offering'
teaches that one may donate oil.
And how much? Three log.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאָמַר שְׁלֹשָׁה לוּגִּין –
phrases.english: And whom have you heard who says three log?
It is Rebbi;
and he derives it from 'offering'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's answer in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that רבי learns from 'אזרח'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא that holds three לוגין, which is רבי, learns from 'קרבן' in the מנחה section.

steps.title: רב פפא accepts the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא admits that if the ברייתא really teaches this, he cannot argue with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If it is taught, it is taught.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives in. He has no answer against an actual ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a concession, not a real answer. רב פפא's 'אזרח' idea falls away, and the explanation in step 18 is left standing.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is taught, it is taught: I accept it

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, רבי learns donated oil from מנחה only to show it can be donated. The rest follows נסכים: three לוגין, all burned.

phrases.english: He said to him: If it is taught, it is taught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב פפא's reply to the challenge in step 21.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא wins. רבי learns from 'קרבן' (מנחה).

steps.title: שמואל: donated wine is sprinkled on the fires
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that someone who donates wine sprinkles it on the altar fires.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: One who donates wine brings it and sprinkles it on the fires.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: שמואל teaches what is done with wine that someone donates on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular נסכים are poured into the basins. שמואל says donated wine is handled differently: it is sprinkled on the fire itself.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
One who donates wine
brings it and sprinkles it on the fires.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from donated oil to donated wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Donated wine is sprinkled on the altar fires.

steps.title: Why is the wine put on the fire?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of שמואל's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what source supports שמואל's rule. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since נסכים normally go into the basins, the גמרא wants to know why donated wine goes onto the fire.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for sprinkling donated wine on the fires

steps.title: The פסוק calls wine an אשה, a fire offering
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק calls wine for a נסך an 'אשה', a fire offering, which shows there is a kind of wine that goes on the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And wine you shall bring for a libation, half a הין, a fire offering, a pleasing smell to ה''.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is 'אשה', fire offering. Since regular נסכים go into the basins, this word tells us there is a kind of wine, the donated kind, that is put on the fire.

phrases.english: The verse says:
'And wine you shall present for the libation, half a hin,
a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to ה׳.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'אשה' shows that some wine goes on the fire.

steps.title: But the wine puts out the fire!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: sprinkling wine on the fire puts it out, and putting out the altar fire is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is putting out the fire!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring liquid on the altar fire would put some of it out. That seems to break the rule that the altar fire must never go out.

phrases.english: But he is extinguishing!
phrases.notes: The Torah forbids putting out the altar fire (ויקרא 6:6).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: Sprinkling donated wine on the fires
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wine on the fire puts it out, which is forbidden on the altar.

steps.title: Partly putting out a fire is not called putting it out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that putting out only part of the fire does not count as putting it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Putting out part of it is not called putting out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and keeps שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is on putting out the altar fire. Sprinkled wine only dampens a small part of it, so it does not count, and שמואל's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Putting out only part of the fire

steps.whatToRemember: Donated wine is sprinkled on the altar fires because of the word 'אשה'. Putting out only part of the fire is not forbidden.

phrases.english: Extinguishing partially
is not called extinguishing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the scope of the prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any dampening of the altar fire is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only putting out the fire counts. Partial dampening is allowed.

steps.title: Taking one coal off the altar and putting it out makes you liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that partly putting out the fire does not count. רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, rules that someone who takes a coal down from the מזבח and puts it out is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: someone who takes a coal down from the מזבח and puts it out is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from the last step, which said that putting out only part of the fire is not considered putting it out. It brings a ruling that putting out even a single coal makes a person liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 said that partial putting-out does not count. But putting out one coal is clearly only part of the fire, and רב נחמן still says the person is חייב. So partial putting-out seems to count after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? An opening word that signals a challenge
Liable, meaning he broke a prohibition

phrases.english: Is that so?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Nachman say in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
One who takes down a coal from on top of the altar
and puts it out is liable,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that putting out part of the fire is not considered putting it out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One coal is only part of the fire, yet רב נחמן makes the person חייב, so partial putting-out does count.

steps.title: That ruling is about the only coal left
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב נחמן's case is one where that coal was the only coal on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, that coal was the only one there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רב נחמן is talking about a case where the coal he put out was the only one, so the whole fire went out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only one coal was on the מזבח, putting it out ends the entire fire. That is full putting-out, not partial. So step 27's rule that partial putting-out does not count still stands.

phrases.english: Where there is only this one!
phrases.notes: The coal he took down was the only coal on the altar, so the whole fire went out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 28
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן seemed to mean that putting out any single coal is forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן means a case where that coal was all that was left of the fire

steps.title: Putting out fire for a מצוה is different
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: even if partial putting-out is forbidden, putting out fire for the sake of a מצוה, like pouring wine, is different and allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say instead: putting out fire for a מצוה is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, separate answer that defends שמואל in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer accepts that putting out part of the fire may be forbidden. It says the sprinkling of wine is still allowed because it is done for a מצוה. That kind of putting-out is treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say, introducing another answer
Putting out fire for the sake of a מצוה

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
extinguishing for a מצוה is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to the challenge against שמואל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any putting-out of the altar fire is forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: Putting out fire as part of a מצוה is allowed

steps.title: Even for the מצוה of removing ashes, one may not put out coals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. Even though the תורה commands removing the ashes, a כהן may not put out coals in order to remove them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב taught: since the תורה said to remove the ashes, you might think one may put out coals and then remove them. The answer is no, he may not put them out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second answer, that putting out fire for a מצוה is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing the ashes is a מצוה. Even so, the ברייתא forbids putting out coals to make ashes for it. That seems to show that a מצוה does not allow putting out the altar fire.

keyTerms.meaning: To remove the ashes from the מזבח (תרומת הדשן)
He shall not put out the fire

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Come and hear, as Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov taught:
since the Torah gave a מצוה to remove the ashes,
might he put out the coals and then remove them?
You say: he shall not put them out!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 30
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that putting out fire for a מצוה is different
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Removing ashes is a מצוה, and still the ברייתא forbids putting out coals for it.

steps.title: There the כהן can just wait
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ashes are different, because the כהן can sit and wait until coals turn to ash on their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because he can sit and wait.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ashes case does not disprove the idea that a מצוה is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the ashes, the מצוה can be done without putting out any fire, because coals turn into ash by themselves if you wait. With the wine, there is no other way to do it, so putting out fire for that מצוה is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is possible, meaning there is another way

phrases.english: It is different there,
since it is possible for him to sit and wait.
phrases.notes: He can wait until some coals burn down into ash by themselves and then remove them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 31
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מצוה never allows putting out the altar fire
steps.terutzMaskana: A מצוה allows it only when there is no other way to do the מצוה

steps.title: ברייתות say wine goes into the basins, not on the fire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings two ברייתות. The first says donated wine goes into the basins while oil goes onto the fire. The second says libation wine goes into the basins and not onto the fire, because of לא יכבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: wine, following רבי עקיבא, goes into the basins; oil, following רבי טרפון, goes onto the fires. And another ברייתא teaches: wine for pouring goes into the basins. Or maybe it goes onto the fires? You say: he shall not put out the fire!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל directly. Sources say donated wine is poured into the basins, not sprinkled on the fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said donated wine is sprinkled on the fire. But a ברייתא says it goes into the basins, while oil goes on the fire. A second ברייתא explains why wine may not go on the fire: it would put the fire out, and the תורה says לא יכבה. That is the opposite of שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Basins on the מזבח where wine was poured

phrases.english: Come and hear:
wine, according to Rabbi Akiva, goes into the basins;
oil, according to Rabbi Tarfon, goes onto the fires!
And it is further taught:
wine for pouring goes into the basins.
phrases.notes: The corrected wording leaves out נסך in round brackets and reads לנסך in square brackets, 'for pouring'.

phrases.english: Or perhaps it goes only onto the fires?
You say: he shall not put out the fire!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: יַיִן כְּדִבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא – לַסְּפָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge against שמואל's original ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule from step 23 that donated wine is sprinkled on the fires
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתות put wine in the basins because pouring it on the fire would put the fire out.

steps.title: This depends on רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, and שמואל follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this follows רבי יהודה, and that follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the ברייתא and שמואל follow two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה forbids an allowed action that ends up causing something forbidden, even when you didn't mean it. רבי שמעון allows it. The person sprinkling wine does not intend to put out the fire, so שמואל, following רבי שמעון, allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: This one ... that one, pointing to two different sources

steps.confusionAlert: Here הא רבי יהודה points to the ברייתא that forbids wine on the fire, and הא רבי שמעון points to שמואל's ruling that allows it.

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
this is Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא that forbids wine on the fire follows רבי יהודה, who forbids even an action where the forbidden result is unintended.

phrases.english: that is Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 33
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is the final word against שמואל
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows רבי שמעון, who allows an action when the forbidden result is not intended

steps.title: Does שמואל really hold like רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether שמואל really holds like רבי שמעון, and brings שמואל's ruling that one may put out a glowing metal coal in a public area so people won't get hurt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that mean שמואל holds like רבי שמעון? But שמואל said: one may put out a glowing metal coal in a public area, so that the public won't be hurt by it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the last answer by bringing another ruling of שמואל. The challenge is still being built and continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last answer depends on שמואל following רבי שמעון. Now the גמרא tests that by looking at a different ruling of שמואל, about putting out a metal coal on שבת. It will check whether that ruling fits with רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: A glowing hot piece of metal

phrases.aramaic: לְמֵימְרָא דִּשְׁמוּאֵל כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ?!
phrases.english: Is this to say that Shmuel holds like Rabbi Shimon?!
But didn't Shmuel say:

phrases.aramaic: מְכַבִּין גַּחֶלֶת שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
phrases.english: one may put out a metal coal in a public area,
so that the public will not be hurt by it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דִּשְׁמוּאֵל כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 34
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמואל holds like רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ruling of שמואל, about putting out a metal coal on שבת, is brought to test whether he really follows רבי שמעון. The argument continues in the next lines.
